text: From Void News, this is On Air. It's Friday, September eighteenth. Canada has answered Washington's tariff threat by moving toward Europe.
Canada's prime minister embraces a first-of-its-kind seat at the European table.
The Federal Reserve raises interest rates for the first time in three years.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has welcomed a proposal to make Canada the European Union's first associate member. The offer comes from European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Carney raised it himself during an official trip that took him from the United Kingdom to Brussels.

Carney says closer ties with Europe would stop any single country from controlling Canada's markets or undermining its sovereignty. He made the case in person to the European Parliament in Strasbourg on Thursday.
Canada has also applied to join the Joint Expeditionary Force, a British-led defense grouping of northern European states.

To the markets. The Federal Reserve has raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point. It is the first increase in three years. The target range now sits between three and three-quarter percent and four percent.
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh says inflation is too high and has been for too long. He says the increase is meant to bring prices back to the central bank's two percent target sooner.
Some outlets lead instead with President Trump's reaction, and with a private phone call between the president and the Fed chairman before the decision.
Now, void opinion. Through a pragmatic lens today. The verdict stands alone, and the listener sits with it.
That's On Air from Void News. Thirty-one tonnes of gold, and a court order that buys the Kennedy Center thirty days. Every source, every story, at Void News.
